clue.text: RN enable fitter to be trained: one to cause embarrassment?

indicators.note: something trained is shaped and reorganised, so the fourteen letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Royal Navy order to train a ship's fitter, apparently a potential troublemaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be trained' rearranges RN, ENABLE and FITTER, all fourteen letters, into the French phrase for a shocking young person.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase literally means a terrible child: someone whose unconventional behaviour embarrasses those around them.

clue.text: Place of opportunity, artist to be engaged in intricate doodle

indicators.note: engaged in means held within, so one piece goes inside the other
an intricate design is complicated and tangled, so the word doodle has its letters jumbled

parts.note: RA, a Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: An artist is caught up in an elaborate doodle of a promised land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intricate' scrambles the doodle and 'to be engaged in' sets the artist inside it; the phrase is Spanish for 'the gilded one'.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary city of gold sought by Spanish explorers, now any place offering great riches or opportunity.

clue.text: Plant? A h-handful's always planted inside

indicators.note: planted inside means set within, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: a stammered 'a f-few', a handful being a few, with the first letter doubled as the stutter on 'h-handful' shows
ever means always, as in 'for ever'

explanation.surface: A stammering gardener says a handful is always planted in among the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter in 'h-handful' is a hint to stutter its synonym as well; 'planted inside' puts the word for always within that stammer.
explanation.definitionFit: A daisy-like herb long used in folk medicine for fevers and headaches.

clue.text: Just that length not as formerly

definitions.meaning: read cryptically: exactly this long and not a bit longer
describes something that used to be so but is not any more

explanation.definitionFit: Read literally, the phrase says something is not longer than it was; idiomatically it means something that has stopped being true.

clue.text: See 1
Last river or brook

parts.note: the last part of something is its end
the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A list of options for the final stream on a map.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last' looks like the definition, since to last is to endure, but it gives END; 'brook' is the verb meaning tolerate.
explanation.definitionFit: To brook something is to tolerate or put up with it, as in 'brook no argument'.

clue.text: Lodger's gossip we hear

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: we hear means the word for gossip is spoken and sounds like the entry

parts.note: gossip is idle talk, rumour

explanation.surface: A lodger's tittle-tattle, as reported to us.
explanation.walkthrough: RUMOUR and ROOMER sound alike in a non-rhotic British accent.
explanation.definitionFit: A roomer is someone who rents a room in another person's house, a tenant.

clue.text: Live musical, not new, put on at the top?

parts.note: to live is to be, to exist

indicators.note: not means take away, here the letter for new

parts.note: Annie is a famous stage musical about an orphan

explanation.surface: A live musical staging, minus anything new, is mounted at the top of the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on at the top?' is a playful definition: something you put on your head. 'not new' takes one N from ANNIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A small brimless knitted hat is worn on the head, so it is something put on at the very top.

clue.text: For instance, part of army pick up issue

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking up lifts the letters so they read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: EG, short for exempli gratia, means for instance
REME, the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, is a corps of the British Army

explanation.surface: For example, a unit of soldiers collects a matter to deal with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pick up' reverses EGREME to give the answer, reading upwards in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue is to come out or flow forth, the verb sense of emerging from somewhere.

clue.text: Society existed in turn to recommend one for the opposition

indicators.note: in turn means turned round, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: to have existed is to have lived
to advocate is to recommend or speak in favour of

explanation.surface: A society that once flourished takes its turn to nominate an opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in turn' reverses S and LIVED together, giving DEVILS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who argues the opposing side for the sake of debate, originally the Vatican official who argued against canonisation.

clue.text: See 9
Repeat broadcasts spread rapidly, kept in reserve

parts.note: RE is the abbreviation for reserve
a dye or rumour runs when it spreads rapidly

explanation.surface: Repeats of programmes quickly circulated, though kept back in reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept in' puts RUNS between R and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Programmes shown again after their first airing are repeats on television.

clue.text: Fine muddle in ship's instructions

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a brig is a two-masted sailing ship

indicators.note: a muddle is a mess, so the word fine is jumbled

explanation.surface: A muddle aboard ship over the orders given to the crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ship's' looks possessive, but just names the vessel; 'muddle' scrambles the fine and 'in' sets it inside the ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A briefing is a meeting where orders and information are passed on.

clue.text: Seen in Nov or in Feb possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Something spotted in November, or perhaps in February.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges the seven letters of OR IN FEB. Bonfire Night is 5 November in Britain, marking Guy Fawkes's failed plot.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonfires are lit across Britain on Guy Fawkes Night, the fifth of November.

clue.text: Warning shout not right for the enemy

indicators.note: not means the letter for right is left out

parts.note: fore is the golfer's warning shout

explanation.surface: A warning cry, but not the right one, against the enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing R from FORE leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A foe is an opponent or adversary in battle.

clue.text: The engine fades, fuel half gone

parts.note: something that fades away dies

indicators.note: half gone means the first half of the word fuel disappears, keeping only its back end

explanation.surface: The motor dies away as the tank is half empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half gone' keeps only the back half of fuel, the second two of its four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A diesel is a compression-ignition engine, or a vehicle driven by one.

clue.text: Sail in a deluge

indicators.note: in tells you the answer is sitting inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A sailor caught out in a downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'a deluge': deLUGe.
explanation.definitionFit: A lug, short for lugsail, is a four-cornered sail hung from a yard.

clue.text: The boasting's cut short

parts.note: boasting or empty talk is often called hot air, and the word for it is a clipped form of gasconade, boastful talk

explanation.definitionFit: Gas means empty talk or bragging, and is also a shortened form of gasconade, extravagant boasting.

clue.text: Disturbance in funfair the cause ?

indicators.note: a disturbance stirs things up, so the letters of funfair are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Who is to blame for trouble at the fair?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disturbance' rearranges FUNFAIR; the whole clue also says who causes the trouble, so it reads as both wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent, lawless thug is just the sort to start a brawl at a fair.

clue.text: English lesson book perhaps in class that's high up

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters might be rearranged

explanation.surface: An English lesson, possibly from a book, in an upper-class schoolroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges LESSON and B into NOBLESS, and E for English closes the word.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for nobility, the aristocracy, the top rank of society.

clue.text: One often well up in heart of dairy business

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle, here the middle letters of dairy

parts.note: a craft is a trade or line of business

explanation.surface: Someone thoroughly versed in the dairy trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well up' looks like 'well informed', but means high in the sky. The middle of DAIRY is AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A plane or helicopter spends much of its time flying high above the ground.

clue.text: Being present at gathering the lady turned up by river

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Netta is a woman's name, standing for the lady
the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales

explanation.surface: A lady comes back up the river to attend a gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses NETTA to ATTEN, followed by DEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who turns up to a meeting or event is a participant there.

clue.text: Elected council vetoes moves when one puts out east

indicators.note: moves means the letters of vetoes are moved into a new order
puts out means ousts, so the letter for one takes the place of another letter

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A council rejects motions after one member throws out the eastern delegate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moves' rearranges VETOES, and one of its Es is replaced by I.
explanation.definitionFit: In Russian the word means council, especially the elected councils of the USSR.

clue.text: Sample of gum -a sticky substance

indicators.note: Sample of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A taste of gum, a sticky material.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across guM A STICky.
explanation.definitionFit: Mastic is a resin from the mastic tree, or a waterproof filler and sealant.

clue.text: Speak again about the bowman

parts.note: re means about or concerning
William Tell, the Swiss archer who shot an apple off his son's head

explanation.surface: Repeat the story about the archer.
explanation.walkthrough: RE followed by TELL.
explanation.definitionFit: To retell is to recount or narrate a story once more.

clue.text: Dicey washer holding the ship in place?

indicators.note: dicey means chancy, as if thrown like dice, so the letters of washer are shaken up

explanation.surface: A risky washer used to secure a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicey' rearranges WASHER. The definition describes what the thing does, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A hawser is a thick rope or cable for mooring or towing a vessel.

clue.text: Burn one's getting from a fight

indicators.note: getting from means leaving, so the letter for one is taken out

parts.note: a fray is a fight or brawl
A means one, as in 'a pound', with the 's standing for 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone gets burned coming away from a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking A out of FRAY leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To fry is to cook in hot fat, or informally to burn in the sun.

clue.text: A state, endlessly flamboyant

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is removed

parts.note: Florida is a US state

explanation.surface: A state without end is showy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the final A of FLORIDA.
explanation.definitionFit: Florid means overly ornate, elaborate or showy in style.

clue.text: Easily controlled fit after a final word

indicators.note: after says the word for fit comes after the closing word

parts.note: amen is the word said at the end of a prayer
able means fit, capable

explanation.surface: Someone fit after a last word seems easy to manage.
explanation.walkthrough: AMEN then ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone amenable is compliant and open to persuasion.

clue.text: Gardener's hat?

parts.note: a bell-shaped cover a gardener puts over young plants, whose name is shared with a close-fitting women's hat

explanation.definitionFit: The French word for bell names both a glass plant cover and a bell-shaped hat.

clue.text: Silver work?

parts.note: a novel featuring the pirate Long John Silver, not something made of the precious metal

explanation.definitionFit: Robert Louis Stevenson's pirate novel features Long John Silver, so it is a book in which he appears.

clue.text: See 28
A certain plant is reduced to ruin by this state car

definitions.text: A certain plant is reduced to ruin by this

parts.note: Colorado is a US state
the Beetle is the classic Volkswagen car

explanation.surface: A state's car that wrecks a certain plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the long opening phrase; the plant in question is the potato.
explanation.definitionFit: A striped leaf beetle is a notorious pest that devastates potato crops.

clue.text: See 30
